column1: # The converter's rules for the hand-written adapters of the rung 1.21 -> 1.20.6 (1.21 names; tabs).
# P <class>                                   a class the adapters provide (in place of carrying it)
# N <class>                                   new above although its intermediary twin exists below (another class)
#                                             an override of a newer method: the mod class gets the interface (the
#                                             adapters' mixins call it from 1.20.4's call sites); a super call into the
#                                             game's own class goes to the defaults method (receiver first)
#                                             a call goes to the adapter's static method (receiver first)
# R <class> <lower class>                     a class renamed below with the same members (NeoForge has no intermediary)
#                                             a field the adapters give: its reads go to the getter (an instance
#                                             field's getter takes the object); with methods, the value's only uses
#                                             a constructor that takes more below (new X(..) and super(..)): each
#                                             lower parameter is an upper one ($0, $1..) or an adapter method's value,
#                                             the method given all the upper arguments; ladder/bottom/<class> names
#                                             the bottom class a top class of the same name hides
#                                             a method that takes more below: each lower parameter is an upper one ($0,
#                                             $1..) or the default written here (false, true, a number, null, or an
#                                             adapter's value "Class.method(this,$k,..)" of the object and upper ones);
#                                             "-" for a lower method without parameters
#                                             the same hook (of the owner and its subclasses) under another name and
#                                             descriptor below; the generated bridges take it from there
# U <owner> <name> <desc>                     a hook the lower game never calls (no counterpart): a mod's override is a
#                                             method of its own below; its calls (super ones too) take the X row
# A <owner> <name> <desc> <lower desc> <plan> the same method below with other parameters: a mixin handler's arguments
#                                             from the lower method's, per upper parameter "$k" (lower k, converted)
#                                             or "Class.method(k,..)" (an adapter of lower parameters k.., and of the
#                                             object: "this"); a mod's override is called by the plan too
# G <folder>                                  a data folder (data/<namespace>/<folder>/) the adapters give a place below:
#                                             the registry they add (its files stay as they are)
# S <owner> <name> <lower desc>               a lower abstract method the upper type hasn't: a mod's concrete class
#                                             under the owner gets an empty one (void, or returning itself)
#                                             a mixin's injection point in that method of the game: 1.20.6's code
#                                             makes the lower call there for the same value (the handler fits both)
# NeoForge 21.1's supportsEnchantment (1.21 asks Enchantment.canEnchant at the anvil, enchant_randomly and /enchant)
# 1.21's DeltaTracker (the frame's time): the client's own from 1.20.6's timer; a partial tick where 1.20.6 passes one
# 1.21's GUI layers take the DeltaTracker where 1.20.6's take the partial tick (the bridges make a DeltaTracker of it)
# 1.21's vertex API: buffers begun by the tesselator, built into MeshData, vertices ended by the next one
# the setters gather the begun vertex's attributes (1.21 takes them in any order; 1.20.6 in its format's)
# recipes: getRecipeFor with the last recipe (1.20.6 gives a pair) and on an input (1.20.6: a container)
# FML 4's config entry points and extension points on FML 3; NeoForge 21's config screen (20.6 has none)
# 1.21's attribute modifier ids (a ResourceLocation; 1.20.6: a UUID and a name)
# NeoForge 21's ItemAbility is 20.6's ToolAction (the same members)
# FollowOwnerGoal: 1.21 asks the animal whether it flies to its owner (TamableAnimal.canFlyToOwner); 1.20.6 takes it as the goal's canFly
# 1.21's use duration with the user (1.20.6: the stack only)
# NeoForge 21's RegisterSpawnPlacementsEvent is 20.6's SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent (the same members)
# 1.21's vertex format elements (record constants) and format builder on 1.20.6's (DefaultVertexFormat's elements, getters)
# 1.21's Leashable and leash data: 1.20.6's mobs (Mob has its members, its leash data its fields); a mod's own leashable
# entity gets 1.21's leash code; a mob's canBeLeashed() is the hook of canBeLeashed(player)
# 1.21 draws a leash in EntityRenderer (render, renderLeash, addVertexPair: the adapters' mixin), turned by the body's yaw of the frame
# NeoForge 21's model locations (a record; a standalone extra model) on 1.20.6's (an extra model under its plain id)
# 1.21's spawn packet with the tracker (ServerEntity; 1.20.6: the entity only)
# 1.21's Model.renderToBuffer without a colour: white (the lower takes the colour's four floats)
# a mod's own VertexConsumer (1.21: addVertex and the setters, a vertex ended by the next): 1.20.6's abstract methods
# small members of 1.21 and NeoForge 21 (fire, damage, sounds, creative tab entries)
# NeoForge 21's damage events, posted from 20.6's (LivingHurtEvent, LivingDamageEvent)
# more small members of 1.21 and NeoForge 21 (enchantments, crossbow, world border, config, attribute maps)
# 1.21's enchantment effects and tags: the curses (1.20.6: enchantment classes; the tags come with the adapters' data)
# 1.21's byte buffers under the builders and buffer sources (1.20.6's builders keep their own memory)
# a buffer source's byte buffers: 1.20.6's builders seen as them (the fixed ones a live map), the shared builder's last type
# 1.21's postHurtEnemy (an item's wear after a hit that counted; 1.20.6's items wear in hurtEnemy)
# 1.21's particle render types (begin with the tesselator, the batch given back; 1.20.6: begin with the builder, end)
# 1.21's server level for an entity's death drops and spawn enchantments (1.20.6: the looting level computed from the blow)
# 1.21's hitbox colour (1.20.6 draws it white), armour foil buffer (1.20.6: of an entity's armour), camera roll (none)
# 1.21's food of an eaten stack, the broken item, the respawn's reason, an arrow's weapon (1.20.6: none of them)
# 1.21's model baking without the model's location (1.20.6 takes it: a placeholder), chunk reading with the region info
# NeoForge 21's QuadBakingVertexConsumer: made empty, its quad asked for (20.6: a consumer of quads); its own vertex setters
# 1.21's GameRenderer.render and renderLevel of the DeltaTracker (1.20.6: the partial tick and the frame's start)
# 1.21's enchantment effects of an attack and an enchantment tag on a stack (1.20.6's post hurt/damage hooks, damage bonus)
# 1.21's portals: the adapters' own (their Entity mixin and portal code use them, a carried copy may be missing from a pack)
# 1.21's dimension transitions (1.20.6: its intermediary twin PortalInfo, a level and a teleporter) and changeDimension
# 1.21's portal tick (its portalProcess and setAsInsidePortal are added to Entity: EntityPortalMixin, PortalSupport)
# 1.21's saddle stack, portal use with passengers, an arrow's weapon (1.20.6: none of them)
# small members of 1.21: the server directory, ARGB colours, an enchantment's full name, paintings in blocks, the tab's
# background, a framed map of a stack, custom data with ops, all enchantments with the registry, a crop's growth speed
# crash reports of a type, chessboard distance to a position, an item parser's patch, the campfire's damage, model baking
# 1.21's render type: sortOnUpload public (1.20.6: private), a finished mesh drawn with the type's state
# 1.21's jukebox songs (a data pack registry and an item component of the adapters'; the jukebox plays them: mixin.Jukebox*Mixin)
# data folders the 1.20.6 adapters give a place (registries they add or fill from data)
# NeoForge 21's names of the target change event's targets
# NeoForge 21's creative tab entries by where they show (20.6's event keeps one map)
# 1.21's GenerationChunkHolder is the generation half of ChunkHolder (1.20.6 has ChunkHolder alone, the same members by other names)
# 1.21's options list of a sub screen (its height is the screen's contents)
# NeoForge 21's damage container and the damage taken event (posted when 20.6's actuallyHurt ends)
# 1.21's BlockAttachedEntity (the base of hanging things and leash knots) is 1.20.6's HangingEntity
# NeoForge 21's event adding blocks to block entity types (posted at the common setup)
# the generation chunk holder's members through ChunkHolder (the R row's class below)
# NeoForge 21's shield block event is 20.6's ShieldBlockEvent (blocked = not cancelled)
# a handler of 1.21's changeDimension(transition) on 1.20.6's changeDimension(level[, teleporter]): the transition to that level
# FML 4's registered configs helper (from FML 3's tracker)
# 1.21's base experience of an entity is 1.20.6's getExperienceReward()
# 1.21's attributes 1.20.6 hasn't (registered by the adapters with their 1.21 ids, used where 1.21 uses them)
# NeoForge 21's config restart types (20.6: a world restart or none)
# NeoForge 21's day time speed of a level (the server's day time advances by it)
# 1.21's dispenser helper and an arrow's weapon
# the registries of 1.21's enchantment effects (made by the adapters with their 1.21 ids)
# B <class>: a carried 1.21 class whose registrations (its bootstrap) the adapters make when its registry registers
# the mods' enchantments as data (registered from their jars by the adapters: DataEnchantments)
# mixin handlers of changed methods: a use duration's user, jigsaw children's liquid settings, a beacon beam's colour
# 1.21's knockback of an attack, a trusted link, the client cookie's report details and server links (1.20.6: none)
# 1.21's model baking without a location: a block model, a model as it is, a top-level model, the missing variant
# a mod's VertexConsumer overriding 1.21's light and posed normal setters (1.20.6: the packed uv2 and the posed normal),
# a mod's BufferBuilder subclass overriding its addVertex
# 1.21's face baking without a model location, arrows with their weapon, the decorated pot sheet's materials, a dye's ARGB
# 1.21's enchantment effect component types (carried; registered into their registry by the adapters)
# 1.21's enchantment loot parameters and sets; a component map codec of other types
# 1.21's effects of an enchantment (a data enchantment's, read with 1.21's effect types)
# 1.21's liquid settings of structure placement (1.20.6 always waterlogs, or keeps liquids by a flag) and dimension padding
# a mod's creative tab with its own background (1.20.6 asks NeoForge's getBackgroundLocation), chunks' persisted status
# a mod's recipe placer moving items to the grid (1.21: a count, the count left; 1.20.6: one item, nothing back)
# 1.21's crafting grid update with the last recipe (1.20.6 looks it up again)
# 1.21's getRecipeFor with the last recipe where the game's own code below asks without it (a mixin's call injectors there)
# NeoForge 21's canSustainPlant of the plant's state with a TriState answer (20.6: of an IPlantable, yes or no)
# 1.21's jigsaw placement with dimension padding and liquid settings (1.20.6: none), and each pool element's own place
# NeoForge 21's c:music_discs item tag (20.6 has the game's minecraft:music_discs only)
# FML 4 loaded config of a mod config (FML 3 keeps its data in the ModConfig)
# a mod's call of 1.21's begin on any particle render type (the game's own types too)
# a checkbox label's wrapping width (1.21; 1.20.6 sizes it to its text)
# NeoForge 21's network codec of a custom holder set type (20.6 syncs holder sets by their codec only)
# a mod level's own day time speed (NeoForge 21's abstract Level methods: 20.6 never calls them; the calls take the X rows)
# 1.21's single pool elements' optional liquid settings (1.20.6's have none): the constructors drop it, the codec field reads it
# 1.21's session search trees (1.20.6: the client's own search registry)
# NeoForge 21's hotbar rendering with the DeltaTracker (20.6: the partial tick)
# 1.21's crash report file as a path, and its saving where 1.20.6's game code saves to a file (a mixin's point there)
# DataFixerUpper 8's build result (DFU 7 builds the fixer itself), 1.21's air block tag, attribute sentiment, multi-line labels
# a mod's own model baker's NeoForge 21 methods (20.6's baking never calls them; the calls take the X rows)
# 1.21's small fireball of a movement vector (1.20.6: its parts)
# the subclasses' own canUsePortal (1.21: LivingEntity's, a throwable's): 1.20.6's canChangeDimensions
# a subclass of 1.21's buffer source (its super call): 1.20.6's of the byte buffers' builders
# 1.21's outline generator record (1.20.6's keeps the colour by channel; made public by the access transformer)
# a handler of 1.21's cloud mesh building (the tesselator; 1.20.6: the tesselator's builder, a rendered buffer back)
# 1.21's check of a link from outside (chat, a book)
# 1.21's sound of a location (1.20.6: its text), the use-item packet's rotation (1.20.6: none)
# 1.21's disconnection of a client with its details (1.20.6: the reason)
# 1.21's camera directions (fresh vectors: a reader may change its copy)
# NeoForge 21's block element face record: its face data, made with a parent holder (1.20.6: set by its element)
# 1.21's model bakery baker: made by a mod (1.20.6's takes sprites by model id), baking a model as it is, its top models
# 1.21's chunk step: its status and write radius, a world generation region's (1.20.6's region keeps them itself)
# NeoForge 21's food tags of one kind (20.6: the plural ones)
# DFU 8's hasResultOrPartial, 1.21's stream codecs of damage types and effects, a damage tag, a list's scroll clamp, weapons
# NeoForge 21's entity level hooks (20.6: the world ones), 1.21's experience drop with the attacker (1.20.6: none)
# 1.21's EnchantmentHelper of effect components: 1.20.6's enchantments for the vanilla effects, the mods' data ones by their files
# 1.21's members of an enchantment on 1.20.6's (the definition's field opened by the access transformer), its mob spawn tag
# 1.21's enchantment stream codec, enchanting table list, vanilla enchantment providers' keys, an arrow's block hit effects
# 1.21's loot builders of an enchantment (1.20.6: looting only, plain numbers)
# 1.21's eating of food properties, food with a remainder, NeoForge 21's primary item of an enchantment (20.6: at the enchanting table)
# 1.21's looting level in its loot functions (getEnchantmentLevel of looting); 20.6's from the loot context (a mod's mixin point)
# a falling block's tick: 1.21 handles portals right after the move, 1.20.6 has no portal call there (a mixin at
# 1.21's portal call goes in just before the move: the tick's same place, one call earlier)
# 1.21's supported item check of an enchantment (a mod's mixin): 1.20.6's canEnchant (calls take the X row)
# NeoForge 21's tool tags, fake player check, the vertex texture element, the frame time of overlay and highlight events
# NeoForge 21's invulnerability check and effect tooltip events (posted by the adapters' mixins on 20.6)
# NeoForge 21's configuration screen comes down as carried code (the adapters give what it reads): a config value's raw
# value and spec, a spec's emptiness, 21's client option of untranslated config warnings
# NeoForge 21's day time of a mod's own level data (20.6 never asks it), the firestarter ability, render buffers of byte buffers,
# 1.21's enchanted books of a creative tab, NeoForge 21's experience drop of a block broken with a tool
# NeoForge 21's item damage with a break callback of the item (20.6: a Runnable)
# 1.21's waterlogging check of structure placement (20.6: keeping liquids, the same flag)
# small 1.21 members: a tame animal's teleport to its owner, an explosion's block triggering, NeoForge 21's holder key (TailAdapters)
